name: Conferences and Positive Notes
title: Conferences and Positive Notes
answer: Conferences and positive notes are two everyday ways teachers communicate with families, and AI can help draft both. A written conference summary gives families a record of strengths, areas for growth and next steps, while a positive note home builds the relationship that makes harder conversations easier later. In both cases the teacher reviews the message, adds the personal substance and decides what is sent.

sections.body: Parent conferences are short, and families often leave without a clear record of what was said. A brief written summary solves that by capturing the child's strengths, the areas for growth and the next steps in a form the family can keep and revisit. Positive notes home address a different problem, which is that many parents hear from school only when something is wrong. A short note about something the child did well keeps the relationship warm, so that a difficult conversation later lands on ground that has already been prepared. The two practices work together as a communication habit rather than a one off event.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: For conferences, a teacher can use an approved tool to draft a brief summary covering the child's strengths, areas for growth and next steps, then review it and send it, translated if needed. For positive notes, a teacher can use AI to help draft a short message and then add a specific detail about what the child actually did well. TalkingPoints makes it easy to send those notes in the family's language. The supplied text does not give grade bands for either practice, so the same approach applies across year groups. In both cases the tool helps with the form and the teacher supplies the substance.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text offers no study, figure or evidence label for this idea, so it rests on practice rather than research. What it does give is the reasoning behind the practice, which is that the personal detail is what makes a positive note work. A generic message saying a child is doing great means little, while a note saying a child helped a classmate solve a hard problem today means a great deal. The claim about conferences is similarly practical, that families often leave a short conference without a clear record of what was said. The text also notes that TalkingPoints makes sending notes in the family's language easy, which is a description of a tool rather than a research finding.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Names and sensitive details should stay out of any tool that is not covered by a signed agreement. The teacher reviews and sends the summary, and the teacher decides what goes into it, so the tool never sends anything on its own. Translation is part of the sending step and remains the teacher's responsibility to check. The substance of a positive note stays with the teacher, because AI can help with the form but cannot know what the child did that day. The judgement about which detail is worth sharing, and whether a note should be sent at all, stays with a person.
